advice.claim: Selling minute sessions or points creates a financial liability because the business owes services to clients who have already paid, whereas recurring membership revenue is an asset.
advice.quote: If you have recurring revenue from memberships, that is considered an asset to your business. You have X amount of dollars that you're expecting in your business. If you have sold minutes, points, sessions, that's a liability.

advice.claim: Recurring membership revenue increases the value of a business when seeking credit or preparing to sell it.
advice.quote: So when it comes time to putting your business in a position to sell, in a business to get credit, it. Say you want to upgrade, you want to purchase new equipment. Having recurring revenue acts as an asset for your business.

advice.claim: Recurring membership revenue reduces owner stress and financial anxiety compared to relying on one-time package sales.
advice.quote: It was July and he walked in the door. I was like, like, hey, buddy, how's it going? And he stretched his arms up and he goes, good. It's July and I'm sleeping like a baby. Because he had revenue. He knew that when he put the key in the door, he had that money coming into his salon.

advice.claim: Membership status creates a sense of belonging that makes clients ignore competitors' advertising.

advice.claim: Offering a high-value product bundle (e.g., $70 worth of product) as a sign-up incentive is more effective than simple discounting.
advice.quote: So if they see that on the counter and they see, well, I can get a $70 worth of product for signing up, that's one reason to sign up, right? So value added.

advice.claim: When transitioning to memberships, keep long-term legacy clients on their old pricing and packages to avoid friction.
advice.quote:
There's a client that's been coming in for 20 years and they always buy the same package
and they always do the thing.
Don't upset the apple cart.
Let them keep doing that.
But every new customer coming in gets this pricing and sees only this pricing.

offer a free spray tan yeah
their membership wave um normally there is a fee to sign up yeah wonderful and then we ended up
getting a few people signing up and nobody ever used the spray tan

advice.claim: The average membership duration is typically four to five months.

advice.quote:
maybe you reward
somebody at the sixth month after their membership maybe it's something small maybe it's a you know
a bottle of a tan extender but at a year let's work out how much that client spent with you
because maybe throwing them a hundred dollar gift card wouldn't be a bad idea

if you're loaded on the bottom end
if you have all 20 minute beds you're not going to sell the higher end

advice.claim: Some lotion brands offer a 10% cash back incentive if the salon carries at least 75% of their product lines.
advice.quote: you can get 10% cash back and that's going to be, we just asked that you carry 75 of our products

advice.claim: Certain lotion brand loyalty programs offer a higher cash back rate (17%) if the salon carries their products and uses their provided social media assets.
advice.quote: then you can also get 17 cash back if you do all of that and then including the advertising which is going to be the social media portion

advice.claim: Rebate checks from some manufacturer loyalty programs can take between 8 to 12 weeks to process once received.
advice.quote: they usually take about eight to 12 weeks. I want to say processing time, you know, once we receive them.

advice.claim: The Premiere program offers a 15% return for participants in the new year.
advice.quote: You just scan it, sign up, and we'll get you 15% back in this new year.
